test.description: mexico-paternal-surname-quirk-first-plan: q_001 has no plan yet, and the localities entry loc_001 already carries a collection quirk from the FamilySearch Wiki (https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Improve_your_Search_Results_for_Hispanic_Ancestors_in_FamilySearch.org). input.delegation:
Create the first research plan for q_001 — who were the parents of María Guadalupe Hernández Ramírez (b. about 1895, Guadalajara, Jalisco, Mexico)?

questionId: q_001
projectPath: <workspace>

judge_context: A `localities` entry (loc_001) is ALREADY in research.json — the orchestrator ran locality-guide before research-plan. The skill should READ that entry and use its quirks; it should NOT call wiki_search / wiki_place_page / place_population (research-plan does not hold those tools). Do NOT fail it for not surveying.

The quirk under test is loc_001's: "Although Mexicans use two surnames, most indexed records carry only the first (paternal) surname — search with the paternal surname alone; when the person is not found, search through the parents (a parent search with each parent's first surname, leaving out the child's name). (FamilySearch Wiki: https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Improve_your_Search_Results_for_Hispanic_Ancestors_in_FamilySearch.org)"

The persisted `plan_items[].rationale` is the only place that counts — narration is not persisted and search-records never sees it. Correctness turns on the plan item that searches Jalisco civil registration (collection 1918187) for her birth: its persisted rationale must state that the index usually carries only the paternal surname (so search 'Hernández', not 'Hernández Ramírez'), and that a parent search is the fallback. A plan whose reply mentions the quirk while that item's rationale does not fails this point. Paraphrase is fine.
Plan items must include rationale explaining why each record type was chosen for the question — generic rationale ('more records would help') is a fail.
